full_judgment:
12. It appears from the impugned judgment that the learned Judge of the High Court Division relying upon the decisions in the case of Ashwini Kumar Karamaker being deed his heirs, Sree Radha Raman Karmaker and others Vs. Hari Mohan and others and Darastuallah and others V.S. Manik Mondal and others reported in 36 DLR (AD) 1 and 88 respectively holding that the Court can rectify an illegality in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction at the instance of the parties or even Suo Motu. However, it must be noted that such exercise of jurisdiction cannot be allowed if it moans giving premium to the inaction of any party. In the instant case, it appears from the evidence on record that the pre-emptee disclosed on 21.07.1985 the names of four persons said to be co-sharers who had been left out. The pre-emptor impleaded those four persons as opposite parties did not name any other person as being necessary party who was left out, there is no obligation on the part of the pre-emptor to implead nay other party and as such the law not bad for mis-joinder or non-joinder of party. 

 "13. All objections on the ground of no joinder or misjoinder of parties shall be taken at the earliest possible opportunity and, in all cases where issues are settled, at or before such settlement, unless the ground of objection has subsequently arisen, and any such objection not so taken shall be deemed to have been waived". 

 14. In the instant case there is no dispute that the parties named by the pre-emptee have been impleaded as opposite party and that no ground was taken either in memorandum of appeal in the Court of Appeal below or the revisional application regarding defect of party. Any such sub-mission made before the revisional Court is, therefore, beyond the pleadings and cannot be a ground for remanding the case to the trial Court for fresh trial. In the case of Abdus Samad and others Vs. Md. Sohrab Ali and others reported in 33 DLR (AD) 113 it was held that if the preempted or any of the parties disclose the existence of necessary parties before trial and the pre-emptor fails to implead him or them his application for pre-emption shall fail. In the case of Matilal Sikder and others Vs. Benodini Dasi, being dead her heirs Bepin Behari Das and others reported in 28 DLR (AD) 5 it was held that non-joinder of necessary party will not be fatal to a pre-emption proceeding and the pre-emptor is only under obligation to implead necessary party provided the pre-emptee furnishes necessary particulars of the necessary party. However, in the instant case it appears that the pre-emptor did implead the parties named by the pre-emptee who had been left out of the pleadings. The provision of Order I Rule 13 is such that all objection regarding non-joinder or misjoinder must be taken at the earliest opportunity, before the settlement of issues and any such objection not so taken shall be deemed to have been waived. 

 15. It appears that the pre-emptor impleaded the parties made by the pre-emptee as having been left out. Therefore, subsequent claim of non-joinder of party cannot defeat the pre-emption.
